0.34.0 original: BLOCK F 0, 12 findings: 4x IH-CRED-001 high = lines 78/79 (commented-out optional EXTEND.md keys `# remote_publish_identity_file: ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, `# remote_publish_known_hosts_file: ~/.ssh/known_hosts`; the skill says only typed keys honored, SSH key auth only) + lines 111/160 (troubleshooting table/setup note saying API credentials go in the skill's own `.baoyu-skills/.env`); 2 NET-001 medium (api.weixin.qq.com, mp.weixin.qq.com), REF-001 low x5, CRED-005 low.
Variants (0.34.0): ssh paths -> /path/to/... only = still BLOCK (env lines); env lines reworded only = still BLOCK (ssh lines); both = REVIEW F57 (NET mediums + lows remain); uncommenting the ssh keys = BLOCK (13 findings).
Class (new): CRED-001 high on a *config key whose value is a key-file path* (pointer to where the user's SSH key lives, for the tool's own ssh -i), inside a commented-out example block — scored like reading/exfiltrating the key. Plus .env-as-storage-location mention (seen before in flipt/pipeline-assistant).
Idea candidates: CRED-001 downgrade when the path is the value of a `*_identity_file`/`*_known_hosts_file`/`IdentityFile` style config key with no read/cat/upload verb and no network sink on the line; skip YAML/markdown comment lines in config examples. Risk: attacker hiding a real read behind a config key; test on MSB/prose/blind sets + look-alikes.
